Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pramod Kumar Sahani Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Sanjeev Kumar,
learned counsel appearing on behalf of Pramod Kumar Sahani, learned counsel for the informant.
By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant, who is involved in Case Crime No. 367 of 2022, under section 376 (3) IPC, Section 3/4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 67 (B) of Information Technology Act, Police Station Ghosi District Mau, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012

sentences.text: As per prosecution case, in brief, informant who is father of the victim lodged a first information report on 16.7.2022 against the applicant with the allegation interalia that the applicant has committed rape on his daughter.

It is further alleged that the applicant, after making her obscene video during the course of the rape also, made the same viral.

sentences.text: It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
As per ossification test report, victim is aged about 18 years and as such she was major.

It is also pointed out that when the victim was produced for her medical examination, she has refused for the same and when her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded, she has not supported the prosecution case.

Referring the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it is pointed out that the victim has clearly stated that she is aged about 22 years and the applicant was known to her since last 3 years.
The physical relations between them was made with the consent of each other.
She has also stated that she wants to marry with the applicant.
Earlier her parents were ready for her marriage with the applicant but later on they refused to do so.
Regarding the alleged obscene video, she has stated that the said video was made with her consent and the applicant did not make the same viral but someone else has made the same viral.
On the strength of the aforesaid facts, it is argued that the victim was major and consenting party.
The applicant has no criminal history and is languishing in jail since 19.07.2022.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant but they could not dispute the factum of the case as argued on behalf of the applicant.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that the date of incident has not been mentioned in the first information report.
Victim has refused for her medical examination and as per the ossification test report she is aged about 18 years.

She has also not supported the prosecution case in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused and submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and also considering the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., as noted above,
possibility of victim being consenting party with the applicant and false implication of the applicant cannot be ruled out, as such, this Court is of the opinion that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant Ram Singh Chauhan be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.

In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail.
It is clarified that anything said in this order is limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything said in this order.
